newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends lower on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends lower on poor demand.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were lower at the close with expectations of large amount of raw materials and a lack of consumer demand undermining sentiment, dealers said.
"There is an ample supply, and demand is lacking. Consumers are not going to buy unless prices fall further to more attactive levels," a dealer said.
He added that trading was routine with business mainly on a hand-to-mouth basis. Some scattered South Korean and Taiwanese interest was seen for SMR grades but they were just checking on the prices.
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 295 cents a kg, SMR CV at 358, SMR L at 338, SMR 5 at 307, SMR 10 at 296 and drum latex FOB at 234.
The increase in raw materials was due to the improved weather conditions, traders said. Some traders said some producers were unwilling to dispose at current levels.
Consumers preferred to divert their interest to other producers like Thailand and Indonesia, dealers said.
At the close, February RSS 1 eased two cents to 299 cents ($1.19) a kg and February SMR 20 was down 1.50 cents at 294.50 cents.
